theorem_title: The parity-compatible refined child reaches the same endpoint
natural_language_statement:
Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$. For natural parameters $L,\varepsilon,z$, put $A=4z+2\varepsilon+1$, $P=2^LA-1$, and $Q=3\cdot2^{L-2}A-1$. When $L<2$, the exponent $L-2$ uses truncated natural subtraction.

Assume $L\ge2$, $\varepsilon\le1$, and $\varepsilon\equiv L\pmod2$. Then

$$
T^L(Q)=\left\lfloor\frac{3^LA-1}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

This gives the child side of the guarded coalescence construction.

formal_statement:
theorem CollatzWork.refinedChild_iter (L epsilon z : Nat) (hL : 2 ≤ L)
    (hepsilon : epsilon ≤ 1)
    (hparity : epsilon % 2 = L % 2) :
    shortcutIter L (refinedChild L epsilon z) =
      (3 ^ L * refinedA epsilon z - 1) / 4 := by sorry
